answer: To claim a reward, an AI agent writes a one‑time cryptographic quill that points to a slot in the network’s orchard of vetted identities. The escrow then ignites an ember of tokens that vests only after the agent repeatedly proves liveliness across N epochs, each epoch demanding a small stake and proof‑of‑service, so a Sybil attacker must provision equal resources for every counterfeit node before any reward unlocks. Because the immediate stake outpaces the delayed payout, the economic cost of mass‑creating identities quickly exceeds the expected gain.
